channel.title: The Porchlight Journal
channel.description: Practical pet sitting, dog walking and pet care advice from Porchlight Pet & Home Care in Belmont, NC.

item.title: Traveling With a Cat on Insulin or Daily Medication
item.description: Cats with diabetes, kidney disease or other conditions can still stay home while you travel. Here is how to plan the schedule, supplies and vet backup.

item.title: My Cat Hides From Strangers. Can a Cat Sitter Still Help?
item.description: A cat who vanishes when the doorbell rings can still be cared for well at home. Here is how a good sitter works with a shy cat, and how you can set them up.

item.title: Can You Leave a Cat Alone for a Weekend? Risks and a Safer Plan
item.description: Cats are independent, but two nights alone can go wrong in ways owners do not expect. Here are the real risks and what a safer weekend looks like.

item.title: How Much Does a Cat Sitter Cost? What Changes the Price
item.description: Cat sitter pricing depends on visit length, number of cats, holidays and overnight stays. Here is how it adds up for a typical trip, with real local numbers.

item.title: Holiday Travel Season: Book Your Pet Sitter Early and Prepare for Thanksgiving to New Year's
item.description: Good sitters book up weeks ahead for the holidays. Here is a timeline for booking, what to prepare, and how to keep pets safe around holiday food and guests.

item.title: Puppy and Kitten Care: What a Sitter Needs to Know Before You Leave
item.description: Young pets need frequent potty breaks, safe play and incomplete vaccines to be handled carefully. Here is how to arrange care for babies.

item.title: Caring for Senior Pets While You Travel: What Sitters Need to Know
item.description: Older pets are wonderful companions, and they need extra planning. Learn what changes with age and how to set up safe, comfortable care.

item.title: Birds, Reptiles, Fish and Small Pets: Care While You're Away
item.description: Exotic pets have specific needs for heat, light, feeding and handling. Here is what to prepare, and what a sitter should know, before you leave.

item.title: Microchips, ID Tags and Escape-Proofing: How to Keep Your Pet From Getting Lost
item.description: A microchip only works if the registration is current. Learn how ID, chips and a few home fixes protect your pet, especially when someone else is in charge.

item.title: Halloween and Everyday Hazards: Foods and Plants That Are Toxic to Pets
item.description: Chocolate, xylitol, grapes, lilies and more. A quick reference to common household toxins, plus Halloween-specific risks for dogs and cats.

item.title: Pet Emergencies: Warning Signs, a First Aid Kit and Your Emergency Plan
item.description: Know the signs that mean "go to the vet now," build a simple pet first aid kit, and set up an emergency plan before your sitter needs one.

item.title: Separation Anxiety in Dogs: Signs, Causes and How a Sitter Can Help
item.description: Is it boredom or true separation anxiety? Learn the signs, gentle ways to help, and what to look for in a sitter if your dog struggles when you leave.

item.title: Caring for Cats While You're Away: How Often Should a Sitter Visit?
item.description: Cats are independent, but they are not self-sufficient. Learn how many visits cats need, what a sitter checks, and how to keep your cat comfortable.

item.title: Fleas, Ticks and Heartworm: Year-Round Prevention for Dogs and Cats
item.description: Mild southern winters mean parasites do not take a break. Here is how prevention works and what your sitter should know about it.

item.title: Dog Walking Basics: Exercise Needs, Harness vs. Collar, and Leash Manners
item.description: How much exercise does your dog need, which gear is safest, and how can you make walks calmer for everyone? A practical guide for owners and walkers.

item.title: Giving Medications While You're Away: A Safe Plan for Pet Owners and Sitters
item.description: Pills, drops, insulin and supplements need a precise plan when someone else is in charge. Here is how to set up a sitter for success.

item.title: How to Write a Pet Care Instruction Sheet Your Sitter Will Actually Use
item.description: A clear one-to-two page sheet prevents most mistakes. Use this template to cover feeding, walks, medications, quirks and emergencies.

item.title: Cat Vaccines and Health Checks to Complete Before You Travel
item.description: Even indoor cats benefit from a pre-trip checkup. Learn which vaccines are considered core, which are optional, and how to hide fewer surprises from your sitter.

item.title: Dog Vaccines Before a Sitter or Boarding Stay: What's Required and What's Recommended
item.description: Rabies, distemper, bordetella and more. Here is how core and non-core dog vaccines differ, and which ones sitters and boarding facilities typically ask to see.

item.title: Pet Sitter or Boarding Kennel? How to Choose What's Right for Your Pet
item.description: Both options can work well. This guide compares in-home pet sitting with kennel boarding so you can match the care to your pet's personality and health.

item.title: Fireworks, Thunderstorms and Noise Anxiety: Keeping Pets Calm and Safe
item.description: July 4th is one of the busiest times of year for lost pets. Here is how to prepare your dog or cat for fireworks and summer storms.

item.title: The Complete Checklist for Getting Your Home and Pet Ready Before an Overnight Stay
item.description: A week-by-week countdown of everything to do before you leave, from vet records and food supplies to the small home details sitters always wish they had known.

item.title: Hot Weather Dog Walking: Pavement, Paws and Heatstroke
item.description: Summer in the Carolinas is hard on dogs. Learn the seven-second pavement test, the early warning signs of heatstroke, and how to keep walks safe when it is hot.

item.title: What to Expect at a Pet Sitter Meet & Greet
item.description: The meet & greet is where trust gets built. Here is what happens, what to show your sitter, and the questions every pet owner should ask.
